draft.title: Writing a thesis
card: A thesis is your answer to the essay question, in one or two sentences. The rest of the essay sets out to prove it.
A thesis must be arguable. This means a reader could disagree with it, so you have to give reasons to persuade them.
A thesis names an idea about the text, not just a topic. A topic is what the text is about, such as friendship. An idea is what the text says about it, such as that friendship can survive hardship.
A thesis answers the question that was asked. It does not retell the plot or only repeat the question.
draft.remember: A thesis is an arguable answer to the question that states an idea about the text.

a.q: Which of these is the strongest thesis for an essay on a novel about a family living through a drought?
opts: The novel argues that hardship can bind a family together
The novel is about a family living through a drought
The novel has a family, a farm and a long drought
Many families face hardship, and this novel shows one
a.why: The first option states an idea about the text that a reader could argue with, so the essay can set out to prove it. The second is tempting but only names the topic, so there is nothing to argue.
a.clue: Which one says something a reader could disagree with?

b.q: Question: How does the poet present memory? Which response is a thesis?
opts: The poet presents memory as a comfort that is also painful
The poet presents memory in several different ways
The poem is about memory and uses many techniques
In the first stanza the speaker remembers her childhood
b.why: The first option answers the question with an arguable idea about how memory is presented. The second is tempting because it echoes the question, but it takes no position and could be said of any poem.
b.clue: A thesis takes a position rather than repeating the question.

a.best: The novel argues that hardship can bind a family together

b.best: The poet presents memory as a comfort that is also painful
